# WH-001 Receiving & Putaway SOP

## 1. Purpose

### 1.1 Objective
This procedure defines how inbound freight is checked in, verified, counted, inspected and put away at the Meridian Supply Co. distribution centre. It exists so that every unit entering the building is traceable to a purchase order and is available for sale or use as soon as practical.

### 1.2 Scope
It applies to all inbound truckload, less-than-truckload and parcel deliveries received at dock doors 1 to 8, including supplier shipments, transfers between sites and customer returns routed through the dock.

## 2. Dock Check-In

### 2.1 Driver and carrier check-in
The receiving clerk logs the carrier name, trailer number, seal number and arrival time in the dock schedule. The seal number is compared with the bill of lading before the seal is broken. A mismatched or missing seal is recorded on the bill of lading and reported to the Warehouse Supervisor before unloading starts.

### 2.2 Door assignment
Doors are assigned in order of appointment time. Hazardous material loads are always assigned to door 8, which is next to the hazmat cage.

## 3. Documentation Match

### 3.1 Matching the ASN to the PO
Before any pallet is counted, the clerk matches the advance ship notice (ASN) to the purchase order (PO) in the warehouse system. The supplier, PO number, item numbers and ordered quantities on the ASN must agree with the PO. A delivery with no ASN, or one that cannot be matched to an open PO, is not received; it is parked in the staging lane and Procurement is called.

### 3.2 Packing slip
The packing slip is compared with the ASN. Differences are noted on the receiving record and handled under the policy in WH-003.

## 4. Count and Inspection

### 4.1 Count
Cartons and pallets are counted against the ASN. Blind counting is used for any line flagged high value. Counts are entered at the dock using a handheld scanner.

### 4.2 Inspection
Each delivery is inspected for the conditions in the table below.

| Check | Action if failed |
|---|---|
| Outer carton damage | Note on bill of lading, photograph, see WH-003 |
| Wet or contaminated packaging | Quarantine and notify Quality |
| Wrong item or lot label | Hold and notify the buyer |
| Missing lot or expiry data | Hold until supplier provides it |

### 4.3 Quality sampling
Items on the supplier watch list are sampled at the rate set by Quality. Failures are handled under QA-001.

## 5. Putaway

### 5.1 Putaway time standard
Received goods must be put away within 4 hours of receipt. Receipt time is the moment the receiving record is closed in the warehouse system. Any pallet that cannot meet this standard is reported to the Warehouse Supervisor, who records the reason and the new expected putaway time.

### 5.2 Location assignment
The system directs putaway to a bin location by item velocity class and size. Operators confirm the bin by scanning the location label and the pallet label. Overrides require supervisor initials.

### 5.3 Staging rules
Goods awaiting putaway are kept in the green-floor staging lane only. Nothing is left in aisles or in front of fire equipment.

## 6. Hazardous Materials

### 6.1 Hazmat to cage zone H
All hazardous material is moved to cage zone H immediately after the receiving record is closed. Safety data sheets must be present before the goods are accepted into the cage. Hazmat is never stored in general racking, and incompatible classes are kept in separate bays inside the cage.

### 6.2 Missing safety data
If the safety data sheet is missing, the load is held on the dock in the marked hold area and the buyer is notified the same shift.

## 7. Records

### 7.1 Receiving record
The receiving record shows the PO, ASN, counts, inspection result, exceptions, clerk name and the receipt time. Records are retained for seven years.

### 7.2 Exceptions
Every exception raised at the dock receives a reference on the receiving record so that it can be tracked to closure.
